messages.subject: Mnumeric issue
messages.body_plain:
Hi all,

Apologies I missed the questions about "Mnumeric".  I have given 2 workshops recently and not seen this, so perhaps the issue has been fixed.  It looks like it is an issue with the Matrix package, or some other package that uses Matrix as a dependency.

If you get errors like this:

===================
tipranges = getranges_from_LagrangePHYLIP(lgdata_fn=geogfn)
Read 2 items
Read 310 items
Error in validObject(.Object) :
   invalid class “tipranges” object: superclass "Mnumeric" not defined in the environment of the object's class
> tipranges
Error: object 'tipranges' not found"
===================

...try switching to a different version of the Matrix package (it may be that the newest versions work also, given that the workshops were OK).

https://stackoverflow.com/questions/69283444/error-in-validobject-object-invalid-class-dsparsemodelmatrix-object-super
===================
remove.packages("Matrix")
packageurl <- "https://cran.r-project.org/src/contrib/Archive/Matrix/Matrix_1.3-2.tar.gz" install.packages(packageurl, repos=NULL, type="source")
===================

("Mnumeric" probably stands for "Matrix Numeric", and perhaps some change to the Matrix package has filtered up to BioGeoBEARS.)

Please report back if something like the above works!

Cheers!
Nick

messages.subject: Comparing different classification schemes in BioGeoBEARS
messages.subject_clean: Comparing different classification schemes in BioGeoBEARS
messages.body_plain:
Hi everyone,

I am studying mouse lemur diversification
      in Madagascar. We use BioGeoBEARS to reconstruct ancestral
      ranges/habitats for the genus. A variety of different habitat
      classifications exists for Madagascar, ranging from binary
      (humid/dry) to more fine-scale ones that distinguish a higher
      number of ecosystem types. We reconstructed ancestral habitats for
      many of them but, ideally, we would also like to test which of
      theses classifications explains mouse lemur diversification best.
      Is there a way to compare modelling results from analyses with
      different classifications (e.g., humid/dry vs. one using more tip
      states such as humid/subhumid/dry)? These classifications are not
      necessarily nested.

Can the AIC (weights) be used for this? I am unsure because a
      different classification is not a model change but a change in
      input data... I searched the google group for an answer to this
      issue but could only find the following rather old entry, which did not resolve the issue: https://groups.google.com/g/biogeobears/c/Jlab5WketCo

Cheers,
Tobias
